race_context: The district: Tell City-Troy Township School Corporation in Perry County runs two schools, William Tell Elementary (pre-K through grade 6) and Tell City Junior-Senior High School (grades 7-12) {idoe_dir}. State enrollment counts were 1,400 students in 2022-23, 1,360 in 2023-24, 1,351 in 2024-25 and 1,322 in 2025-26, down from 1,425 in 2018-19 {idoe_enroll}. The state directory lists John Scioldo as superintendent {idoe_dir}.

The board has five members: Tony Thomas (president), Larry Goffinet (vice president), Hanna Fortwendel (secretary), Ross Hendershot and Derek Kleemann {tc_board}. Goffinet nominated Thomas to continue as president at the board's Jan. 13, 2026 reorganization meeting, and the board agreed unanimously {pcn_jan}. Members are elected at large in staggered groups: state results show three seats filled in 2018 and three in 2022, while the 2020 and 2024 races drew fewer candidates than seats, and in 2024 the only winner listed was Tony Thomas, as a write-in {enr_2018}{enr_2020}{enr_2022}{enr_2024}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three at-large seats, matching the state list's 'vote for 3' {in_list}. They are the seats won in 2022 by Hanna Fortwendel, Ross Hendershot and Larry J. Goffinet {enr_2022}. Fortwendel and Goffinet are running again; Hendershot is not on the ballot, so at least one seat will go to a newcomer. Blair Walsh and Ike Glenn are the two challengers {in_list}{ic_list}.
Name note: the district website and the 2022 state results spell the incumbent's name 'Hanna Fortwendel', the same as the 2026 ballot list {tc_board}{enr_2022}{in_list}.
Facilities: on April 14, 2026, the board awarded the contract for a new fieldhouse (auxiliary gym) on the high school campus to Jasper Lumber, the lowest fully compliant bidder {pcn_field}.

Staffing and budget: on July 14, 2026, the board approved new administrative contracts after promoting Chris Hollinden to principal and Nick Weyer to assistant principal. The Perry County News reported that even with the raises, the district will save about $20,000 in administrative costs {pcn_admin}. In September 2025 the board again approved supplemental pay for teachers who earn dual-credit qualifications or a master's degree {pcn_teach}.
Special education: on Sept. 8, 2026, the board approved plans to keep special education services in-house as much as possible because the Exceptional Children's Co-op is dissolving {pcn_sped}.

Budget and SEA 1: this guide did not find a full, freely available account of how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district. The district held a public hearing on its 2027 budget on Sept. 8, 2026 {tc_budget}. This guide found no operating or safety referendum for the district.

Forums: the Perry County News held a political forum on Oct. 5, 2026, announced as featuring Democratic and Republican candidates {pcn_forum}; this guide found no report that school board candidates took part. It found no questionnaire, voter guide or campaign website for any Tell City-Troy candidate.
